Every time someone upvoats one of your comments, you get a Comment Contribution Point (and lose one if someone downvoats, but you're safe from that here). Because Voat wants to encourage participation and discourage lurking, you need these for some stuff.

  • Comment Contribution Points (CCP) are different from Submission Contribution Points (SCP). CCP has more effects.
  • You get 1 voat in a 24 hour period (not a calendar day) for every 2 CCP you have (your voats = your CCP / 2), but there is a minimum of 10 (at 20 CCP).
  • You cannot downvoat until you hit 100 CCP.
  • Votes are associated with your IP address. That means you cannot vote on the same post or comment using alternate accounts, or if your roommate already voated. Only the first vote will be counted.
  • Only the 10 upvoat (before 20 CCP) and downvoat capability (100 CCP) limits are checked by your browser. They are the only ones that show you a notification. If you are over those, but out of voats your voat will be silently ignored and disappear on reload. It is also not checked by the mobile app.
  • The checking done on the server side lags by at least an hour. You will likely be able to voat more than your limit.
  • If you go below -50 on either CCP or SCP, you get severely limited on how much you can post.
  • If you downvoat more than you upvoat, you are branded a "VotingMeanie" and not allowed to downvoat until you fix it.

I've pulled most of these directly out of Voat's code on Github. The rest are from experiments I ran.

It means you and your roommate can't voat on the same thing. A decent number of cell phone companies out there put everyone behind a multi-ip NAT. It's a good one where it'll keep you on the same IP for all the transactions with a single site, but that times out in a while and the next time you show up your external IP will be different (and possibly one that someone already used).

And it does little to stop spam bots because VPNs are cheap. I see it as similar to DRM on software, it can annoy legit users while the bad guys can work around it easily.

I have a feeling Voat's openness is going to make it harder to fight against spammers. It's easier to work around measures you can see. Of course security through obscurity isn't actual security, but it does mitigate when your security is bad.
